title: Configure ESP-IDF for the bottle cap after a wake source was asked for on a pin that cannot wake the chip

steps.note: the request: the fuel gauge's ALRT (u6, on IO6) as a Deep-sleep wake source
the firmware configuration has not been generated in this copy

instruction: The smart bottle's cap board (module bottle-cap-board, src/boards/bottle-cap) needs its ESP-IDF firmware configuration generated and exported; the copy you have has none yet. The firmware owner has just added the fuel gauge's alert as a Deep-sleep wake source in firmware.config.ts, so the cap can warn about a low battery. Produce fresh firmware outputs so that `npx protoboard check` reports no errors and no firmware finding left open. The board is already fabricated: do not change the board module, its circuit config or its circuit outputs. Tell me what you generated and what the firmware owner needs to know about their wake request.

graders.description: the invalid wake source is gone and the answer says why (IO6 is not an RTC GPIO, only GPIO0-5 wake the chip)
the button wakes the chip; the alert is still configured as an input on IO6, not as a wake source

solution.say: The fuel gauge's ALRT reaches the ESP32-C3 on IO6 (u1:pin_20), and only the RTC GPIOs GPIO0-5 can wake the chip from Deep-sleep, so firmware:check refused it (FW_WAKE_INVALID). GPIO0-5 are all in use and the board is fabricated, so I removed u6 from the wake sources (the button sw1 on GPIO3 stays), generated and exported: out/config/board_pins.h and sdkconfig.defaults with the manifest. The alert is still configured as an input (BOARD_U6_ALRT_GPIO, IO6, active low) for when the chip is awake; a low-battery wake needs the next board revision to route ALRT to an RTC GPIO, or the firmware can poll the gauge on each timer wake.
